title: The Spectrum Lab
summary: Order the electromagnetic spectrum, classify waves by wavelength and find frequencies and photon energies.
subject: physics
learningOutcome: The student can order the bands of the electromagnetic spectrum, find the frequency and photon energy of a wave from its wavelength, and explain that all of them share the same speed in vacuum.

levels.title: Put them in order
levels.adds: Baseline: the bands run from radio waves to gamma rays as wavelength falls and frequency rises (Section 8.4).
hints: Radio waves have the longest wavelengths, gamma rays the shortest.
Visible light sits between infrared and ultraviolet.
Pick them from the longest wavelength down.

levels.title: Name that wave
levels.adds: New idea: place a wavelength in its band and use f = c/λ (Ex 8.3).
hints: Compare the wavelength with the typical size of each band.
f = c/λ, with λ in metres.

levels.title: Photon energies
levels.adds: New idea: the photon energy is E = hf = hc/λ, in eV (Ex 8.9).
hints: E = hc/λ in joules, then divide by 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹.
A shorter wavelength means a more energetic photon.
You can type tiny energies like 2.5e-9.

levels.title: The same speed
levels.adds: Apply it: every electromagnetic wave travels at c in vacuum, whatever its wavelength (Ex 8.3).
hints: X-rays, light and radio waves differ in frequency, wavelength and photon energy.
Only one quantity is the same for all of them.

misconceptions: Radio waves travel more slowly than light
X-rays travel faster than visible light
All electromagnetic waves have the same frequency in vacuum
